newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - March 12.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - March 12.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A survey has found that Australian executives are increasingly having to meet performance targets before they are given share options. The survey, conducted by share and option advisory firm Equity Strategies, showed that of Australia's top 100 firms in 996, 67 per cent linked the incentive to pre-established performance hurdles. Page 5.

A resolution between Kerry Stokes' Seven Network Ltd and his hostile partners in Optus Vision over the control of the cable-TV company looks possible within 48 hours following secret negotiations between Optus Vision partners - including Optus Communications, US West and Publishing & Broadcasting. Page 19.

Thanks to his record in boosting the once flagging Big W, Woolworths Ltd deputy managing director Roger Corbett is the institutional investors' favourite to replace Chris Tideman as David Jones chief executive after Tideman's resignation on Monday, just days before the release of the upmarket retailer's interim results. Page 19.

A multimillion dollar study into the feasibility of taking the 40 million carat a year Argyle diamond mine from open pit to underground operation will be presented to the main partners, Ashton Mining Ltd and RTZ-CRA, on Thursday, but a formal decision on the ambitious plan is not expected until April. Page 21.

BHP Co Ltd yesterday signed a A$3 million three-year joint venture deal with exploration minnow Platsearch NL to seek Broken Hill or Cannington-style silver-lead-zinc ore-bodies in the Curnamona crator region, which lies on the New South Wales - South Ausralian border. Under the agreement, BHP is committed to 3,000 metres drilling in the first year and a further 2,000 metres each year for the next two years. Page 21.

Despite the release of drilling results yesterday described by Helix Resources management as pleasing and exciting, analysts are still concerned by the depth and low-grade nature of gold assays from the explorer in the last few months, and Helix has yet to convince the market it has an economic gold mine at Tunkillia in South Australia. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following the release of the Productivity Commission's controversial draft report on the future of Australia's automotive industry, which called for a reduction in tariffs from 15 per cent in 2000 to five per cent in 2004, Ford Australia president David Morgan joined other business and political leaders in attacking the report, saying it was both "mischievous and misleading". Page 31.

Almost 60 years after turning its back on its birthplace to expand into global markets, BHP, Australia's biggest company, is to return to Broken Hill, where it will spend A$2.5 million to explore the 550 square kilometre Mundi Mundi silver, lead and zinc enements over three years under a farm-in deal with PlatSearch NL and Savage Resources Ltd. Page 31.

After David Jones revealed on Monday its chief executive Chris Tideman would be resigning for "personal reasons" and returning to the United Kingdom, the embattled department store is tipped to announce a replacement for the top job this week as the company unveils its interim profit. Page 31.

In a move representing the first break for some time in the pay-TV deadlock, which has prevented Optus, Foxtel and Australis Media from making much progress in the struggling industry, Optus Vision shareholder Seven Network Ltd may begin selling its top-rating sports programming to Foxtel, which could end the on-going legal dispute with Optus. Page 31.

In the latest conflict since supermarket giant Woolworths Ltd last month announced its move into the A$10 billion-a-year wholesale grocery market - Davids Ltd's traditional wholesaling area - Davids yesterday predicted Woolworths would come off second best from the move and would lose money from its decision. Page 33.

Despite fears that its break last year with the De Beers diamond cartel would lead to a price war, diamond producer Argyle Mining Ltd has posted a 57 per cent rise in operating profit from A$16.5 million to A$26.1 million in the year to December 31, thank to an increase in sales diamond sales from the Argyle mine in Western Australia, which Ashton has a 40 per cent interest. Page 33.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

David Jones shares rose three cents to A$1.74 in response to the surprise resignation of the company's chief executive, Chris Tideman, yet the department store's board has been put on notice by institutional shareholders to implement strategies to revive earnings and its strategic direction amid fears the half-year result, to be released today, may be worse than expected. Page 29.

Coca-Cola Amatil chairman Dean Wills has moved to reassure investors in the 1996 annual report, issued yesterday, by saying weaker results for the year to December should not obscure longer term plans, and predicting a return to the double-digit profit growth experienced two to three years ago. Page 29.

Sydney-based mining house RGC, one of the world's largest tin producers, believes its mining activities are on the verge of substantial growth as governments respond to environmental concerns and legislate against the use of lead bullets and shot. Page 29.

Wholesaler Davids has suffered a 17.4 per cent drop in net profit to $A24.15 million in the December half, but management is still aiming to tackle Woolworth's expansion into the independent wholesale distribution market. The fall was due to costs associated with the purchase of QIW and a disappointing performance by Campbell's Cash & Carry divison. Page 31.

Investment bank NatWest Australia has lifted its net profit 40.8 per cent to $A68 million for 1996. Favourable financial markets conditions and big-ticket corporate financing were the impetus for the profit gain, in a year which saw the All Ordinaries inex rise 15 per cent. Page 31.

Seven Network and Optus Vision shareholders have given themselves another 48 hours to reach settlement over the legal action which threatens the ownership structure of the cable group. On Friday three shareholders were legally obliged to transfer their shares in Optus Vision over to Seven, however this deadline passed, and talks are still continuing. Page 31.
THE AGE

Following the surprise resignation of David Jones managing director Chris Tideman on Monday, the upmarket retailer is expected to announce his replacement when it posts its interim figures, which are tipped to show a sharp drop in profits. The list of candidates to replace Tideman appears limited to local retailers. Page B1.

Argyle diamond mine partner Ashton Mining has posted a December profit of $A26.1 million for the year. These figures are up from $A16.5 million the previous year, but included a first-time equity-accounted contribution of $A5.5 million from the 32 per cent-owned Aurora Gold. Page B3.

Lower gold prices and increased costs have seen Resolute Ltd post a December half profit which fell $A5 million. Profit fell to $A15.1 million, down from $A20.1 million, despite production rising by 30 per cent. Page B3.

Sydney-based mining house RGC is poised for substantial growth as governments outlaw lead bullets and shot. One of the world's largest tin producers, RGC is also likely to receive further boosts to productivity as manufacturers of technical equipment such as mobile phones are forced to use tin instead of lead for soldering of electrical components. Page B3.

Helix Resources plans to release a preliminary estimate for its gold discovery in Area 223 of South Australia's remote Gawler Craton by June. The discovery caused a mini-boom in Gawler exploration stocks, yet has since met with fading enthusiasm due to the gold's low grade, the 50 metre overburden present, and its remote location. Page B3.

Figures compiled by life insurance industry consultants Rice Kachor Research show the life insurance industry has scored big increases in premium income, with annual income up 29 per cent and single-premium income jumping 48 per cent compared to the previous September quarter. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
